questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to go on exchange in Italy to improve my Italian. But since my Italian is not quite good enough for academic purposes I also needed there to be some courses in English that could substitute some obligatory courses at KU

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It can be quite hard to find the information you need. But the Erasmus Office in Pavia responded to all my emails and answered all my questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were two welcome seminars during the welcome week, which were informative. But to be honest a lot of the time you just had to learn by doing. And take it a bit as it comes.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: With my specific program if was quite frustrating the lack of information - especially about the schedule, classes and so on.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite hard to find since a lot of people only want students who can stay for at least a year. But I think that if you go through the university it is easier. One option could be to check out Airbnb and try to make a long-term deal with the landlord outside of the website. I also know a lot of people who found housing when they got to Pavia, but it made the intro-period quite stressful it seemed.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The city is very small so even though you are off campus you are very close to everything. Some of the on-campus sites are quite far from the city center and I would really recommend to live in the city center!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I mainly found the process difficult because I had very specific courses I needed to make sure I could take. But the registration itself went very smoothly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus Office was very helpful and you can also sign up for a buddy, who can help you set settled.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did a lot of research beforehand so I ended up getting all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Have patience! sometimes you want things to happen a bit faster, but it is Italy! ;) 
And then just write to the Erasmus Office with questions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The main problem was the logistics. It seemed like the program I was in was quite a mess. So not a lot of information. Things would change - time and place. We got information in the last minute. But the courses and teachers were generally good. However I am doing my Bachelor and exclusively had classes from the master program - and it seemed to me like the level was a lot lower than at KU.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was not high! I only had classes on Masterlevel and these were very easy. A lot of them very introductory.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was primarily frontal lectures and not a single discussion or group exercise. We wrote a lot of abstracts as an exercise.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Cognitive development
Experimental Psychology
Neuroeconomics
Neurolinguistics
Psicologia della cognizione sociale

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really enjoyed Psicologia della cognizione sociale, but that is mainly because of personal interest. 
I also joined some Practical Lab Courses from the program, which was really interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not as far as I remember

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Eating out was really cheap! Books from the bookstore the same. Cross-country traintickets were cheap too. 
The rent was actually a bit more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think there were quite a few. But I myself did not use them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was an university sports club with all sorts of cool sports. There was an outdoor club. And then ESN had all sorts of events and trips you could sign up for.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to participate in the welcome week activities! very easy way to make friends! Also check out events outside of ESN to meet Italians and not just other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: TRAVEL! Even though the local trains can often be late, the long-distance trains are amazing and connect all of Italy. From Milan you can reach so many places!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The most difficult was having dinner late.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Uh that is more difficult. But If you try to speak some Italian to them you are definitely one step ahead.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Actually the more laissez faire attitude to schedules, time and planning was quite hard to get used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The socializing, going out, meeting friends, having dinner, having drinks, drinking coffee-thing! <3

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Prepare yourself for some chaos and lack of organization
2. Everything will eventually sort itself (maybe you need to send one or two emails) out
3. Enjoy!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The above.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of nice people, eating amazing food, traveling in Italy off-season, newfound appreciation for my home university

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The lack of organization and cancelled trains

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: In the end every challenging thing was worth it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
